labware.title: The wrong kind of plate: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat is a flat plate, and Cloning needs a PCR plate or PCR strips
labware.explanation: The plate map says the technique is Cloning, which needs a PCR plate or PCR strips as its destination. The protocol delivers into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 3, load name nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat), which is a flat plate. A thermocycler block is drilled for thin-walled 0.2 ml PCR wells; a flat plate does not fit in it, so the reaction can never be run. The plate map checks what each well holds, not what plate it is.
labware.fix: Load nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt (or the 200 ul PCR plate, or PCR strips on the aluminium block) as the destination; a flat plate cannot go in a thermocycler.

protocol.py: 4 biology problems (3 warnings, 1 note).

1. WARNING COLD-MODULE-NEVER-SET: A temperature module was loaded but never set
   line 45:  p300_multi.aspirate(30, block["B1"])  # aspirate 30 µL buffer
   At line 45 the robot draws from wells A1, A9, A10, A11, A12, B1, C1, D1 and 4 more in
   slot 1, on a temperature module that the protocol never sets. A temperature module stays
   at room temperature until `set_temperature` is called, so buffer (carrier), enzyme
   (reagent), plasmid 1 (sample), plasmid 10 (sample) and 11 more sat on a block that was
   never cold; the robot pipetted there 8 times over the run. The person setting up the deck
   sees a module and assumes it is cold. Wells: wells A1, A9, A10, A11, A12, B1, C1, D1 and
   4 more in slot 1.
   Affected: wells A1, A9, A10, A11, A12, B1, C1, D1 and 4 more in slot 1.
   Fix: Call `temp_module.set_temperature(4)` before the first transfer from Opentrons 96
   Well Aluminum Block with Generic PCR Strip 200 µL in slot 1, and
   `temp_module.deactivate()` at the end.
   Source: Opentrons, temperature module: at room temperature until set_temperature, which
   blocks
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/temperature_module.html
   Source: Thermo Fisher T4 ligase manual: keep on ice, use within minutes
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/t4dnaligase_1U_man.pdf
   Source: NEB: Q5 High-Fidelity PCR kit manual (add the polymerase last)
           https://www.neb.com/-/media/nebus/files/manuals/manuale0555.pdf
   [a0386b497d7d]

2. WARNING ENZYME-BEFORE-DILUENT: An enzyme was added before the water: enzyme
   line 47:  p300_multi.dispense(2, plate[f"A{i}"])
   At line 47 the robot put enzyme into wells B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, B7, B8 and 4 more in
   slot 3 (this line did it 12 times). Take well B1 in slot 3: at that moment it was dry,
   and the water came afterwards, at line 54, to make the 1 ul of water or buffer the
   reaction is built on. An enzyme is shipped in 50% glycerol and is meant to be the last
   thing into a reaction, after the water and the buffer have brought the well to the right
   dilution. Dropped into neat buffer or a dry well it meets many times the salt it should:
   a restriction enzyme then cuts at the wrong places (star activity) and a polymerase
   starts on mis-primed template.
   Affected: wells B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, B7, B8 and 4 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Reorder the additions to wells B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, B7, B8 and 4 more in slot 3:
   water and buffer first, then the sample, then enzyme last. Or make a master mix of water,
   buffer and enzyme in one tube, mix it, and hand it out.
   Source: Thermo Fisher: restriction enzyme key considerations (the enzyme is the final
   component)
           https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/life-science/cloning/cloning-learning-center/invitrogen-school-of-molecular-biology/molecular-cloning/restriction-enzymes/restriction-enzyme-key-considerations.html
   Source: Promega: restriction enzyme resource (add the enzyme last; glycerol and star
   activity)
           https://www.promega.com/resources/guides/nucleic-acid-analysis/restriction-enzyme-resource/
   Source: NEB: Q5 High-Fidelity PCR kit manual (add the polymerase last)
           https://www.neb.com/-/media/nebus/files/manuals/manuale0555.pdf
   Source: Qiagen: critical factors for successful real-time PCR (order of addition)
           https://www.gene-quantification.de/qiagen-qpcr-sample-assay-tech-guide-2010.pdf
   [eb59089b76ec]

3. WARNING UNMIXED-AT-END: 4 wells never mixed after plasmid 9, plasmid 10, plasmid 11 and
plasmid 12 went in (26% of the well)
   line 74:  p20_single.dispense(5, plate[f"A{i}"])  # dispense 5 µL into destination well
   At line 74 the robot added plasmid 9, plasmid 10, plasmid 11 and plasmid 12 to wells A9,
   A10, A11 and A12 in slot 3, which already held buffer and water (this line did it 4
   times). The addition was 26% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run
   ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so
   what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. The liquid added last is
   a sample, so nothing else in the workflow will mix it: a normalisation or a pool left
   like this is not what it says it is.
   Affected: wells A9, A10, A11 and A12 in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix wells A9, A10, A11 and A12 in slot 3 after line 74: `mix_after=(5, 15)` on the
   transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 15, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well
   holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [4b55f2ce87cd]

4. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: Well E1 in slot 3 never mixed after the liquid from well E1 in slot
1 went in (25% of the well)
   line 67:  p300_multi.dispense(5, plate["A1"])  # dispense into the 2x4 block of destination wells
   At line 67 the robot added the liquid from well E1 in slot 1 to well E1 in slot 3, which
   already held the liquid from well F1 in slot 1, the liquid from well G1 in slot 1 and the
   liquid from well H1 in slot 1. The addition was 25% of the well, nothing mixed the well
   afterwards, and the run ended with it that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do
   not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated.
   If the plate is vortexed and spun down before it is used, nothing is wrong; if it goes
   straight to the instrument, the wells are not what the protocol says they are.
   Affected: well E1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix well E1 in slot 3 after line 67: `mix_after=(5, 16)` on the transfer, or
   `pipette.mix(5, 16, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [3c76fd391c22]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

findings.explanation: At line 45 the robot draws from wells A1, A9, A10, A11, A12, B1, C1, D1 and 4 more in slot 1, on a temperature module that the protocol never sets. A temperature module stays at room temperature until `set_temperature` is called, so buffer (carrier), enzyme (reagent), plasmid 1 (sample), plasmid 10 (sample) and 11 more sat on a block that was never cold; the robot pipetted there 8 times over the run. The person setting up the deck sees a module and assumes it is cold. Wells: wells A1, A9, A10, A11, A12, B1, C1, D1 and 4 more in slot 1.
findings.fix: Call `temp_module.set_temperature(4)` before the first transfer from Opentrons 96 Well Aluminum Block with Generic PCR Strip 200 µL in slot 1, and `temp_module.deactivate()` at the end.

findings.title: An enzyme was added before the water: enzyme
findings.explanation: At line 47 the robot put enzyme into wells B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, B7, B8 and 4 more in slot 3 (this line did it 12 times). Take well B1 in slot 3: at that moment it was dry, and the water came afterwards, at line 54, to make the 1 ul of water or buffer the reaction is built on. An enzyme is shipped in 50% glycerol and is meant to be the last thing into a reaction, after the water and the buffer have brought the well to the right dilution. Dropped into neat buffer or a dry well it meets many times the salt it should: a restriction enzyme then cuts at the wrong places (star activity) and a polymerase starts on mis-primed template.
findings.fix: Reorder the additions to wells B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, B7, B8 and 4 more in slot 3: water and buffer first, then the sample, then enzyme last. Or make a master mix of water, buffer and enzyme in one tube, mix it, and hand it out.

findings.title: 4 wells never mixed after plasmid 9, plasmid 10, plasmid 11 and plasmid 12 went in (26% of the well)
findings.explanation: At line 74 the robot added plasmid 9, plasmid 10, plasmid 11 and plasmid 12 to wells A9, A10, A11 and A12 in slot 3, which already held buffer and water (this line did it 4 times). The addition was 26% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. The liquid added last is a sample, so nothing else in the workflow will mix it: a normalisation or a pool left like this is not what it says it is.
findings.fix: Mix wells A9, A10, A11 and A12 in slot 3 after line 74: `mix_after=(5, 15)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 15, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.

findings.title: Well E1 in slot 3 never mixed after the liquid from well E1 in slot 1 went in (25% of the well)
findings.explanation: At line 67 the robot added the liquid from well E1 in slot 1 to well E1 in slot 3, which already held the liquid from well F1 in slot 1, the liquid from well G1 in slot 1 and the liquid from well H1 in slot 1. The addition was 25% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with it that way.
